subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw own a stable interoperability protocol for independent non-Node and bare-metal agent runtimes?
rationale: The current release provides reusable private TypeScript code and an experimental trusted-plugin harness, but a cross-language protocol would create a new durable compatibility, security, and support commitment.

options.title: Sponsor Protocol RFC
options.body: Define a minimal versioned event, tool, session, model, and capability contract with conformance tests on a constrained reference runtime.

options.title: Remain Node-Hosted
options.body: Keep Node and an operating system as the supported runtime boundary and treat MimiClaw-style ports as independent adaptations.

options.title: Limit To Plugin RPC
options.body: Support non-TypeScript implementation code only through the narrower plugin process boundary tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98004.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Protocol RFC
recommendation.body: Define a minimal versioned event, tool, session, model, and capability contract with conformance tests on a constrained reference runtime.

likelyOwner.reason: Direct issue participation and authorship of the agent-core internalization make this the strongest available decision-owner signal.
